"""Emit the mounted CD's directory tree (names, sizes, mtimes) as cdrom.js.
Root README.TXT and AUTORUN.INF are embedded byte-for-byte; other files are metadata only."""
import base64, json, os, sys
root, out = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
EMBED = {'README.TXT', 'AUTORUN.INF'}
def walk(p, top):
    ents = []
    for name in sorted(os.listdir(p)):
        fp = os.path.join(p, name); st = os.stat(fp); t = int(st.st_mtime * 1000)
        if os.path.isdir(fp): ents.append([name, t, walk(fp, False)])
        elif top and name.upper() in EMBED:
            ents.append([name, t, None, st.st_size, base64.b64encode(open(fp, 'rb').read()).decode()])
        else: ents.append([name, t, None, st.st_size])
    return ents
label = os.path.basename(os.path.normpath(root))
with open(out, 'w') as f:
    f.write('// Directory tree of the mounted %s CD. Generated; file bodies omitted except root README.TXT and AUTORUN.INF.\n' % label)
    f.write('window.W95CD = ' + json.dumps({'label': label, 'tree': walk(root, True)}, separators=(',', ':')) + ';\n')
EOF

"""Recompile the Windows 95 system modules that run natively under the 16-bit personality (ne16.js) and
write system.js: original file bytes, translated wasm and metadata for each, plus the shared table of
16-bit import thunks. Usage: build_system.py SYS_DIR OUT.js"""
import base64, json, os, subprocess, sys, tempfile
src, out = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
here = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
b64 = lambda p: base64.b64encode(open(p, 'rb').read()).decode()
# NE modules, in dependency order: (file, load base, first selector, block-table base)
NE = [('gdi.exe', 0x01C00000, 0x1007, 0x06A00000)]
# 32-bit system DLLs: (file, load base, block-table base)
PE = [('gdi32.dll', 0x01D00000, 0x06C00000)]
bundle = {'ne': {}, 'dlls': {}, 'thunks16': []}
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
    reg = os.path.join(tmp, 'registry.json')
    for f, b, sel, lk in NE:
        p = os.path.join(src, f); base = os.path.join(tmp, f)
        subprocess.run([sys.executable, os.path.join(here, 'recomp.py'), p, base, '--base', hex(b), '--selbase', hex(sel),
                        '--lookup', hex(lk), '--registry', reg], check=True)
        meta = json.load(open(base + '.json'))
        bundle['ne'][meta['name'].upper()] = {'file': b64(p), 'wasm': b64(base + '.wasm'), 'meta': meta}
    bundle['thunks16'] = json.load(open(reg))['thunks']
    for f, b, lk in PE:
        p = os.path.join(src, f); base = os.path.join(tmp, f)
        subprocess.run([sys.executable, os.path.join(here, 'recomp.py'), p, base, '--base', hex(b), '--lookup', hex(lk)], check=True)
        bundle['dlls'][f.upper()] = {'file': b64(p), 'wasm': b64(base + '.wasm'), 'meta': json.load(open(base + '.json'))}
with open(out, 'w') as fh:
    fh.write('// Generated by tools/build_system.py from the Windows 95 system files.\nwindow.W95SYSTEM = ')
    json.dump(bundle, fh, separators=(',', ':')); fh.write(';\n')

# Scripting the shell

`window.win95` drives the running shell through the same paths a person uses: pointer events on the screen
canvas and keys through the shell's key handler. It is the same in the Electron app (DevTools protocol on
`127.0.0.1:9334`, `Runtime.evaluate`) and in a browser tab (`http://localhost:8095`).

Coordinates are screen pixels of the emulated display, origin top left. `win95.screen()` gives the size.

## Input

| Call | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `move(x, y)` | moves the pointer |
| `click(x, y, { button: 'right', double: true })` | press and release; both options optional |
| `dblclick(x, y)` | two clicks inside the double-click time |
| `down(x, y, o)`, `up(x, y, o)` | one half of a click, for custom gestures |
| `drag(x1, y1, x2, y2, steps = 8)` | press, move in steps, release |
| `type(text)` | each character as a key; `\n` is Enter |
| `key('alt+F4', 'tab', 'enter')` | named keys with `ctrl+`, `shift+`, `alt+`, `meta+`; names: `enter`, `esc`, `tab`, `backspace`, `delete`, `up`, `down`, `left`, `right`, `home`, `end`, `pageup`, `pagedown`, `space`, `F1`..`F12`, or a character |

Dialog mnemonics (`&Yes`, `&No`) are not handled by the shell's dialogs yet: use `tab` and `enter`, or click.

## Windows and menus

| Call | Returns |
| --- | --- |
| `windows()` | `[{ title, x, y, w, h, active, minimized, maximized, modal }]`, bottom to top |
| `window(title)` | the topmost window whose title equals the string or matches the RegExp, or `null` |
| `activate(title)` | brings it to the front, restoring it if minimized |
| `close(title)` | closes it as its close box would |
| `menus()` | the open menus, each a list of item labels without `&`, `-` for separators |

## Programs and files

| Call | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `run(command)` | what Start > Run does with the command line |
| `open(path)` | opens a folder window or the file's program |
| `saver(path)`, `stopSaver()` | runs a screen saver full screen, ends it |
| `fs` | the file system (`readText`, `writeFile`, `readdir`, `stat`, ...; see `fs.js`) |

## State

| Call | Returns |
| --- | --- |
| `screen()` | `{ width, height, taskbar }`, `taskbar` the top row of the taskbar |
| `screenshot()` | the screen as a PNG data URL |
| `state` | menus, modals, pointer capture, active window title |

## Example

---
name: run-originals
description: In the Win95 project, run the original Windows 95 binaries (recompiled) instead of re-creating their behaviour in JS
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

When a shell feature exists in a Windows 95 binary (NOTEPAD.EXE, USER.EXE's EDIT control, COMDLG32.DLL, EXPLORER.EXE, SHELL32.DLL), recompile and run that binary rather than writing a JS imitation.

**Why:** A hand-written Notepad editor was stopped with "instead of reinventing text editing, look at the source" and "what isn't being recompiled that requires this feature?" (rhetorical) (2026-10-14).

**How to apply:** Before building a feature, find which binary implements it and route through the recompiler (tools/recomp.py, ne16.js for 16-bit). JS stays for the personality layers (KERNEL, host glue) only. Related: [[gaps-from-evidence]].

---
name: no-checkpoint-stops
description: On long Win95 work, keep going until the task is done; do not end turns for progress reports
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

Do not stop to report progress partway through a long task. Keep working until the asked-for result exists; only stop when blocked on a decision that is genuinely the person's.

**Why:** A mid-task status report on the native USER bring-up got "You weren't told to stop. Keep going. Don't interrupt me again." (2026-10-14).

**How to apply:** Treat "keep going" as standing for the current task. Short one-line progress notes between tool calls are fine; ending the turn is not. Related: [[additions-no-permission]].

---
name: no-writes-through-symlinks
description: "Win95 scratchpad shims: rm a symlink before writing a wrapper in its place; `cat >` writes through to the target"
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

Before writing a wrapper script over a PATH shim in a scratchpad bin/ directory, `rm` the existing entry first. Never redirect (`cat >`, `>`, `tee`) onto a path that may be a symlink to a system file.

**Why:** On 2026-10-14 session 985053b8 ran `cat > hist/bin/python3` where hist/bin/python3 was a symlink to /Library/Frameworks/Python.framework/Versions/3.11/bin/python3. The write replaced the real python3.11 launcher with a wrapper that exec'd itself, so every `python3` on the machine looped, the overseer PreToolUse hook (python) timed out, and all tool calls were blocked until the launcher was rewritten by hand.

**How to apply:** For shims use `rm -f bin/X; cat > bin/X`, or check `[ -L bin/X ]` first. Any wrapper's exec target must be a different file than the wrapper's own resolved path. Related: [[iterate-in-dev-page]].

---
name: next-audio-dialup
description: "Win95 queue as of 2026-10-14: 1) native audio I/O, 2) dial-up over an emulated 56k modem, then Network Neighborhood; then resume native Notepad/dialog bug-squashing"
metadata:
  type: project
---

Order of work (set 2026-10-14, before compaction):

1. **Audio, native.** Recompile the CD's sound stack, not a JS imitation: MMSYSTEM.DLL (16-bit), WINMM.DLL (32-bit) and a Sound Blaster driver (e.g. SB16 from the CD). Emulate the card's I/O ports and DMA in ne16.js portIO (like the ET4000 adapter) and play the DMA buffer through WebAudio. SHELL32 already does LoadLibraryA("winmm.dll"), which now fails (no WINMM).
2. **Dial-up.** Emulate a 16550 UART on COM1/COM2 in ne16.js portIO (COMM.DRV is already native) with a Hayes AT modem at 56k pacing, bridged over a WebSocket to a small local bridge process (Node, started alongside the dev server / Electron) that terminates PPP and forwards to the host network. A network adapter is explicitly not wanted ("not in the spirit of the era"). Check first which parts of Dial-Up Networking (RNAAPP, RNA*.DLL, PPPMAC/VxDs) are Win32/Win16 code that can be recompiled versus VxD code needing a host stand-in.
3. **Network Neighborhood** after dial-up.
4. Then resume: native Notepad/file-dialog bugs. Open item: file Paste stays disabled because SHELL32 needs OLE32 ("Shell IDList Array" never reaches the clipboard); asked whether to add OLE32.DLL from the CD, no answer yet.

**Why:** priorities stated directly ("two priorities next ... 1) audio (native i/o) and 2) dial-up support").

**How to apply:** follow [[run-originals]] (recompile binaries; JS only for hardware/host glue), [[iterate-in-dev-page]], [[drive-via-js-api]].

State at handoff: dev server win95 on :8095 (preview tab-10); Electron app rebuilt via `sh electron/build.sh` and reloaded over CDP :9334. Recent native additions to tools/build_system.py: VER.DLL (WIN95_12 ver.new), LZEXPAND.DLL, VERSION.DLL. Debug aids: `proc.runHook` (per-dispatch), `TRACE_NE=<MODULE,...>` build + `window.W95BTRACE` (per-block) to find guest spins.

git add ne16.js && git commit -q -m "Delete from a file dialog no longer freezes

KERNEL32 #51 (W32S_BackTo32), which USER32's callback relays go through, ran
its target as a nested call, so the delete confirmation's modal loop could not
give up the processor and spun. It now runs as a continuation through a return
thunk, like the other 16/32-bit transitions.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>" && git add win95.js && git commit -q -m "Shell Recycle Bin uses the Windows 95 INFO format

SHELL32 writes C:\\RECYCLED\\INFO as Windows 95 does (20-byte header, 118h-byte
records); the shell kept its own text index in the same file, so neither saw
the other's entries. The shell now reads and writes the binary format (and
still reads its old text index), so files deleted from a native program's
file dialog appear in the Recycle Bin and Empty Recycle Bin clears them.
